title: introduce-soft-evacuation-sentinel-and-staged-kv-veil
author: Sanjay Krishnan
description: Motivation: During a regional spike incident we observed repeated KV drain cascades that amplified latency spikes and caused noisy SLO violations for tail-heavy tenants. This PR introduces a soft-evacuation sentinel (a lightweight coordinator) plus a staged KV-veil policy that preserves critical KV prefixes while admitting a bounded fraction of requests during high tail latency windows. Goals: reduce cascading KV drains, smooth regional failovers, and give SLO-enforcer a predictable backstop without hard-denying traffic. Design summary: - soft-evacuation-sentinel: central small-state controller per region that coordinates soft evacuations instead of immediate full KV drains; emits events to the SLO enforcer and the routing layer; supports epoched quiet windows and a short probation timer for reopen. - staged-kv-veil: a policy layer applied during sentinel-initiated windows that preserves configured KV prefixes (default: user-metadata, customer-config maps) and applies admission fractioning for non-critical prefixes. - latency-tracer hooks: lightweight sampling to relate request path, preserved KV prefix, and observed token-latency to feed the SLO heatmap. - feature gate and rollout: sentinel and KV veil are behind a runtime feature-flag (runtime.enable_soft_evacuation) and default disabled for existing customers. We perform a phased rollout: internal canary -> opt-in team pilot -> region canary -> global rollout. Compatibility/rollback: default behavior unchanged; KV-veil policy requires an allowlist; rollback flips feature flag off and drains sentinel state gracefully. Testing: unit coverage for coordinator state machine, synthetic integration test simulating KV drain churn, canary e2e that verifies no hard rejects and preserved KV prefixes under induced load. Operational changes: adds two new metrics (sentinel.evacuations, kv_veil.preserved_prefix_hits) and two traces. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] tests added - [x] telemetry wired - [x] canary run plan included - [x] docs drafted (ops-runbook) Rollout note: start with a single non-critical region, monitor sentinel.evacuations and slo.latency_99.9; if >2x baseline for 10min automatically flip runtime flag off via rollback script.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) sentinel: core orchestration + state machine; 2) kv-veil: policy implementation, admission fractioner and allowlist; 3) tests/telemetry: integration harness and canary infra + docs and runbook updates
diff_snippets:
+ // KV veil admission fractioner: admit up to N% of non-preserved prefixes
+ if rand.Float64() < cfg.AdmissionFraction { admit() } else { queueOrDegrade() }
review_conversation: Maya Chen (reviewer): This looks promising. Two questions: 1) how do we avoid long-running probation windows causing state blowup? 2) can the admission fractioner be tenant-scoped so we avoid under-serving high-SLA tenants?

Author (Sanjay): Probation defaults to 30s and we cap concurrent epochs per-region to 3; both are configurable. Admission fractioner is tenant-aware; default behavior applies allowlisted tenants with overrides via runtime policy per-tenant.
Jorge Alvarez (reviewer): Please add a safety switch in the helm chart that disables the sentinel by default for Dedicated clusters. Also ensure the security-scan passes for the new proto.
Author: Added helm values toggle and revised proto to adhere to our proto lint rules; security-scan output attached below.

Priya Desai (approver): Verified integration test locally against the simulated KV backend; observed preserved prefixes had <5% additional latency while non-preserved paths were rate-limited gracefully. Approving for canary.
Maya Chen: Left a minor nits around logging verbosity at debug level; not blocking.
release_notes: Introduces a soft-evacuation sentinel and a staged KV-veil policy to reduce cascading KV drains and smooth regional failovers. Defaults disabled; opt-in via runtime flag. New metrics: sentinel.evacuations, kv_veil.preserved_prefix_hits. Ops runbook included.
testing_notes: Canary run performed in us-west-2 with one non-critical region for 3 hours; observed 40% reduction in KV drain events during induced spike, no hard rejections. Synthetic workload harness included under tests/integration.
operational_impact: Low by default (feature gated). When enabled, expect modest increase in telemetry cardinality and two additional metrics to watch. Rollback script provided to disable feature quickly.
notes_for_release_team: Add runtime.enable_soft_evacuation to the runtime flag docs and the Dedicated default helm values; schedule a 1-week canary window and validate sentinel.evacuations and slo.latency_99.9 trends before region-wide enablement.
